answer: Each action can be accepted only after an agent locks a scarce, slashable bond and a randomly chosen peer attests to the same outcome; repeated attestations between the same identities carry less weight. A juniper routing task might require evidence checked by peers across a delta of independent neighborhoods, with basalt records making bonds and slashing auditable. A sybil attacker can mint identities cheaply, but cannot cheaply multiply locked capital or control independent peers: failed or collusive attestations forfeit bonds, while each new identity also dilutes its own influence.
